retro-reflectivity is an important property of a surface exposed in sunlight, which is rarely taken into consideration for urban planning and building envelope design.

retro-reflectivity can be effectively used as a strategy to mitigate the urban heat island, and that a novel analytical model is proposed to describe the angular solar reflectance of retroreflective materials.
the use of retro-reflectors on building surfaces can significantly reduce the urban heat islands, and that the use of a novel analytical model can be a useful tool for the design of urban surfaces.

the assessment of the cooling potential of retro-reflectivity for urban heat island reduction.
the development of a new model for the angular reflectance evaluation of retro-reflecting surfaces, which can be used to estimate their potential to mitigate the urban heat island.
the development of an innovative approach to reduce the urban temperature and the urban heat island.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a retro-reflective material as coating of urban paving and building envelopes would reduce the solar radiation absorption, and consequently the temperature of the surface, with the effect to reduce the urban temperature.
retro-reflectivity is a useful property to be applied in urban planning and design, in order to reduce the overheating effect of the urban environment.
the use of retro-reflectors in urban paving and building surfaces could be a valid solution to reduce urban overheating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
retro-reflectivity is a very promising feature of urban paving and building envelopes for the mitigation of urban heat islands.
retro-reflecting films can be considered a valid solution to mitigate the urban heat island phenomenon, and to reduce the cooling demand of buildings.
the proposed model can be used as a tool for the design of retro-reflecting surfaces for urban heat mitigation and for the estimation of the energy saving potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular reflectance is a key parameter for the evaluation of the optic-energetic behavior of retro- reflective materials.
the solar reflectance of a surface is not a fixed value, but it depends on the angular incidence of solar radiation, and it could be significantly increased by using retro-reflective coatings.

the angular reflectance should be taken into account in any optic-energy analysis of the building envelope and urban paving, as it is the main parameter affecting the cooling potential of retro-reflecting surfaces in the urban environment.
